}}'''Andrei Evgenievich Gusev''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Андрей Евгеньевич Гусев}}, born 27 October 1952) is a Russian writer and journalist. He is the author of 10 inventions, 23 published scientific works.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web |url=http://gusev.webs.com/Bio-en.htm |title=Biography of Andrei E. Gusev |access-date=5 April 2016 |archive-date=9 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209165220/https://gusev.webs.com/Bio-en.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> One of his co-authors is a winner of the Nobel Prize, a legend of the Soviet physics, the academician [[Alexander Prokhorov]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.findpatent.ru/byauthors/1190233/ |title=Патенты автора ГУСЕВ АНДРЕЙ ЕВГЕНЬЕВИЧ |access-date=4 September 2016 |archive-date=17 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317212222/http://www.findpatent.ru/byauthors/1190233/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Andrei Gusev was born in former [[Soviet Union]], in Moscow. His parents were engineers. His father Evgeny Gusev was born in Chernihiv Oblast of Ukraine; his mother Rosalind Maltseva was born in Moscow.<ref name="Rodovid">{{Cite web |url=https://en.rodovid.org/wk/Person:1166195 |title=Andrei E. Gusev in Rodovid |access-date=5 November 2020 |archive-date=19 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119230740/https://en.rodovid.org/wk/Person:1166195 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Andrei Gusev graduated the [[National Research Nuclear University MEPhI|Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] in 1975. The next eleven years he worked as a scientific employee (a medical physicist) in public health services. Also in these years he received a medical education.<ref name="VIP">{{Cite web |url=http://viperson.ru/people/gusev-andrey-evgenievich |title=Andrei E. Gusev on VIPERSON.ru |access-date=16 March 2016 |archive-date=23 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323001300/http://viperson.ru/people/gusev-andrey-evgenievich |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Andrei E. Gusev in 2009.jpg|thumb|right|220px| Andrei Gusev in Moscow, 2009]] 
In 1990 Andrei Gusev became a correspondent of the daily "[[Moskovskij Komsomolets]]". Later he worked as the special correspondent of the All-Russia "[[Rossiyskaya Gazeta]]" and dep. editor-in-chief of the youth newspaper "Stupeni".<ref>НА ПОРОГЕ  XXI ВЕКА, Всероссийский ежегодник, М., "Московский Парнас", 2002 (с.92)</ref><ref>Всероссийский ежегодник НА ПОРОГЕ  XXI ВЕКА, М., "Московский Парнас", 2006 (с.85)</ref>

Since 1993 Andrei Gusev serves as editor-in-chief of [[New Medical Gazette|"The New Medical Gazette"]] (published in Russian).<ref>[http://nmgazette.narod.ru/ "The New Medical Gazette" («Новая медицинская газета»)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302140746/http://nmgazette.narod.ru/ |date=2 March 2014 }} (in Russian)</ref>

Andrei Gusev is the author of several hundreds articles in "[[Moskovskij Komsomolets]]", "[[Rossiyskaya Gazeta]]", "[[Sovetskaya Rossiya]]", "[[Vechernyaya Moskva]]", "[[The Moscow News]]", "Stupeni", [[New Medical Gazette|"The New Medical Gazette"]], magazines "Auto M", [[:ru:Столица (журнал)|"Stolitza"]], "Yatt" etc.<ref name="Bio"/>

Within work in "Stupeni" the first books of the writer were published: a collection "[[Ticket to America (short stories)|Ticket to America]]" (1992) and "[[Presentation (short stories)|Presentation]]" (1993). Then he published "[[Mister Novelist]]" (1994), "[[With Chronos' Permit]]" (1995), "The Russian Story" (1996)  and also the story collection "[[On the Edge of Magellanic Clouds]]" (1998).<ref name="VIP"/> He published his novels "The Painter & Eros" and "Role Plays" in 2003 and  "[[The World According to Novikoff]]" in 2006.
In his prose in the 2010s Andrei Gusev developed the themes of [[BDSM]] subculture in Russia.<ref>[https://mliterature.narod.ru/Wife.htm  The story “The Writers’s Wife Likes BDSM” («Жена писателя играет в BDSM»)]  — on  the site of public fund "Union of Writers of Moscow", 2016 {{in lang|ru}}</ref> Themes include [[Dominatrix|female domination]], [[Bondage (BDSM)|bondage]], [[spanking|erotic spanking]] and [[BDSM]] fiction.<ref>[http://proza.ru/2016/03/10/50  «Русский писатель обожает role plays» (“The Russian Writer Loves Role Plays”)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329054427/http://proza.ru/2016/03/10/50 |date=29 March 2016 }} —  a novel by Andrei Gusev {{in lang|ru}}</ref><ref>[http://lady.webnice.ru/forum/viewtopic.php?t=21732 Повесть «Жена писателя играет в BDSM» (“The Writers’s Wife Likes BDSM”)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215025643/http://lady.webnice.ru/forum/viewtopic.php?t=21732 |date=15 February 2017 }} — in Lady's Club, 2016 {{in lang|ru}}</ref><ref>[https://lady.webnice.ru/forum/viewtopic.php?t=22336 Повесть «Консуммация в Момбасе» (“Consummation in Mombasa”)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609223657/https://lady.webnice.ru/forum/viewtopic.php?t=22336 |date=9 June 2020 }} — in Lady’s Club, 2017 {{in lang|ru}}</ref><ref>[https://gusev.webs.com/Malindi.htm  “Our Wild Sex in Malindi”] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009210533/https://gusev.webs.com/Malindi.htm |date=9 October 2020 }} —  a novel by Andrei Gusev {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

Andrei Gusev served as a prototype<ref>Анатолий Макаров [http://old.cultradio.ru/doc.html?id=520936 "Диалог ума и сердца"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727194612/http://old.cultradio.ru/doc.html?id=520936 |date=27 July 2014 }}, "Радио Культура", 19 октября 2013 г.</ref> for one of the main characters – Andrei Lebedev, a journalist of the newspaper ''Moskovskij Bogomolets'', which is very similar to the famous ''[[Moskovskij Komsomolets]]''  – in the thriller novel ''[[Journalists (novel)|Journalists]]'' by [[Sergei Aman]].  In the novel by the same author ''[[Everything Will Be Okay, We're All Going to Die!]]''<ref>''Аман С.'' «Всё будет хорошо, мы все умрём!» Эротическо-героический эпос. — М.: ИД «Флюид ФриФлай», 2018. — {{ISBN|978-5-906827-70-8}}</ref> Gusev was described under his own name, as a journalist Andrei Gusev.

==Personal life==
Andrei Gusev lives in Moscow. He was married twice and divorced twice. His first wife, Nina Guseva (née Odnoletko), worked as a nurse; his second wife, Ivetta Sarkisyan, is a philologist by training. He has two daughters.<ref name="Rodovid"/>  
His hobby is beekeeping.
